name: Apostle Islands Ice Caves
unique: In rare cold winters, Lake Superior freezes solid enough to walk to sea caves hung with curtains of blue ice, a phenomenon that may not happen at all in a given year.
buzz: When it opens, it is one of the most spectacular things in the Midwest; check the park's ice report before driving. Never go alone.

name: EAA AirVenture
unique: Ten thousand aircraft and 600,000 people descend on a regional airport for a week of airshows, homebuilts, warbirds and a night show with fireworks.
buzz: Even casual visitors are stunned; bring earplugs and comfortable shoes. Lodging books a year out.

name: House on the Rock
unique: A fever dream house built over a chimney, with the world's largest carousel, a sea monster, automated orchestras and a bookcase that opens into a tunnel.
buzz: People either call it a masterpiece of outsider art or a hoarder's monument; both are right. Allow three hours minimum.

name: Devil's Lake
unique: A spring fed lake between two quartzite bluffs, with a balanced rock trail, purple quartzite cliffs and some of the best top rope climbing in the Midwest.
buzz: The bluff trails are crowded on summer weekends; go at sunrise and swim after. The East Bluff is the classic loop.

name: Milwaukee Art Museum
unique: A museum with a winged addition by Calatrava that opens and closes over the lake, plus a strong American and folk art collection.
buzz: The wings opening is the photo, and the collection is solid. Check the schedule for the brise soleil.

name: Door County
unique: A peninsula of cherry orchards, fish boils, lighthouses and limestone cliffs, with a shoreline that feels like Maine and a pace that feels like 1955.
buzz: The fish boil at a Scandinavian restaurant is the ritual; book a cottage months ahead for fall color.

name: Taliesin
unique: Wright's own home and studio, built into a Wisconsin hillside with the roof lines following the ridge, rebuilt twice after fires.
buzz: The house tour is excellent and the estate walk is worth the extra; photography rules are strict. Pair with House on the Rock for whiplash.

name: Lambeau Field
unique: The only community owned team in major American sports, with a stadium tour that includes the tunnel, the frozen tundra and a hall of fame.
buzz: The tour is excellent even for nonfans; game day tickets require a season ticket waiting list or luck.

name: Olbrich Botanical Gardens
unique: Sixteen acres of gardens with a Thai pavilion, a rose garden, a prairie and a conservatory.
buzz: The Thai pavilion is the photo and the outdoor gardens are free. Quiet and pretty.

name: Peninsula State Park
unique: A 3,700 acre park on Green Bay with a lighthouse, a beach, bike trails and a view of the Door County islands.
buzz: The Eagle Bluff lighthouse and the bike loop are the highlights. Book camping early in summer.

name: Summerfest
unique: Eleven stages on the Lake Michigan shore for eleven days, with a giant American flag, fried cheese and a lineup that runs from hip hop to polka.
buzz: It is cheap for a major festival and the lake breeze saves it; headliners cost extra. Bring a blanket and pace yourself.

name: Wingspread
unique: A late Frank Lloyd Wright house with a four winged plan around a central great hall, built for the Johnson wax family.
buzz: For Wright fans it is a major house, and the great hall is the showpiece. Tours by reservation.

name: Yerkes Observatory
unique: The observatory that housed the largest refracting telescope in the world, with a terra cotta ornamented building and a 40 inch lens.
buzz: The telescope and the building are the tour and the restoration is ongoing; tours are limited and book out in summer.

name: Forevertron
unique: The largest scrap metal sculpture in the world, a 300 ton time machine built from industrial salvage by a former junkyard artist, surrounded by giant birds and a teapot orchestra.
buzz: It is free, enormous and completely unexpected; photographers love it at sunset. A ten minute detour off the interstate.

name: Circus World Museum
unique: The winter quarters of the Ringling brothers, with circus wagons, a big top and daily performances in summer.
buzz: The wagon collection is enormous and the shows are real. Good for kids and nostalgia.

name: Harley-Davidson Museum
unique: The archive of an American icon: prototype engines, a wall of gas tanks, the first serial number bike and a room of custom choppers.
buzz: Even nonriders enjoy the design story; the factory tour in Menomonee Falls is a separate booking.

name: Horicon Marsh
company: US Fish and Wildlife Service and Wisconsin DNR
unique: The largest freshwater cattail marsh in the country, where Canada geese stage by the hundred thousand in fall and pelicans nest in summer.
buzz: The auto tour and the visitor center are the easy way in and the fall goose migration is the spectacle; bring bug spray.

name: Cave of the Mounds
unique: A limestone cave with colorful mineral formations, a guided tour and a fossil dig outside.
buzz: The formations are colorful and the tour is easy. A good rainy day stop with kids.

name: John Michael Kohler Arts Center
unique: An arts center with a major collection of artist built environments, plus galleries and studios, free and in a former Kohler family house.
buzz: The art environments are the reason curators visit and it is free; the center runs a residency program in the old factory.

name: Kohler-Andrae State Park
unique: A Lake Michigan beach backed by sand dunes and a boardwalk through a marsh, with a campground in the pines.
buzz: The beach and the dune boardwalk are the family stops; the water is cold and the dunes are fragile, so stay on the paths.

name: Villa Louis
customer: History people, families, house tour fans
unique: A Victorian mansion on a mound above the Mississippi, with original furnishings, a fur trade history and a formal garden.
buzz: The house and the river setting are the tour and the annual car show on the grounds is the local event; it is one of the best historic houses in the state.

name: Wisconsin State Capitol
unique: A granite capitol with the only granite dome in the country and a mural by Edwin Blashfield, on the isthmus between two lakes.
buzz: The dome and the observation deck are the reasons to go up; tours are free and the Saturday farmers market on the square is the local ritual.

name: Wisconsin State Fair
unique: A state fair famous for cream puffs, cheese, livestock shows and a midway, eleven days in August.
buzz: The cream puffs are the ritual and the livestock barns are the real fair. Go on a weekday.

name: Madeline Island Ferry
unique: A ferry from Bayfield to Madeline Island, the largest of the Apostle Islands, with bike rentals, a beach and a state park at the landing.
buzz: The crossing and the island bike ride are the day and the ferry carries cars; the island is quiet and the water is cold.

name: Miller Brewery Tour
unique: A tour of the old Miller brewery with the caves, the brewhouse and a tasting at the end.
buzz: The caves and the history are the interesting parts, and the tasting is generous. Book ahead.

name: Paine Art Center
customer: Art people, gardeners, house tour fans
unique: A Tudor revival mansion with a formal garden, showing art in the family rooms and hosting a holiday lights event that fills the grounds.
buzz: The house and garden are the visit and the holiday show is the local tradition; it is small and the art rotates.

name: Rib Mountain State Park
unique: One of the highest points in the state with a 60 foot observation tower and ski runs on the same hill, above the Wisconsin River.
buzz: The tower view in fall is the reason to climb and the ski hill is a local winter spot; the trails are steep and rocky.

name: Rotary Botanical Gardens
unique: Twenty acres of themed gardens on a former dairy farm, with a Japanese garden, a children's garden and a holiday light show.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the winter lights are the two seasons; it is small and cheap and the paths are flat.

name: Wisconsin Dells Duck Boats
unique: A WWII amphibious vehicle drives straight from the street into the Wisconsin River and up a sandstone gorge, with a driver who tells terrible jokes.
buzz: It is exactly as silly as it sounds and kids love it; the Dells is a waterpark town with a strange natural core.

name: Chippewa Valley Museum
unique: A museum with an indoor pioneer street, a farm kitchen and a gallery on the Ojibwe and the lumber camps, in a park on the Chippewa River.
buzz: The street scene and the farm are good with children and the Ojibwe gallery is the serious part; it is cheap and quiet.

name: Civil War Museum
unique: A museum on the war from the perspective of the upper midwest, with a 360 degree film and a gallery on the home front and the soldiers' letters.
buzz: The film and the personal stories are the reasons to come; it is a good companion to the larger battlefields.

name: Fairlawn Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 42 room Queen Anne mansion built by a lumber and ore fortune, with original woodwork and a view over Lake Superior.
buzz: The house is the tour and the story of the family is the interest; it is well kept and the guides are local.

name: History Museum at the Castle
unique: A museum in a castle-like 1920s Masonic temple with a gallery on Harry Houdini, who grew up in Appleton, and a room on the paper industry.
buzz: The Houdini exhibits are the reason people come and the building is the setting; children like the escape room style displays.

name: Monona Terrace
unique: A Frank Lloyd Wright designed convention center on Lake Monona with a rooftop garden and a curving ramp that was finally built 40 years after his death.
buzz: The roof garden and the lake view are free to visit and the Wright story is the interest; the building is a good rainy day walk.

name: Lincoln-Tallman House
customer: House tour people, Lincoln fans, families
unique: An Italianate mansion where Abraham Lincoln stayed in 1859, with period rooms and a tower view over Janesville.
buzz: The Lincoln room and the house's scale are the tour; the volunteers tell the story well and it is cheap.
